title: The turn that compaction ate
intro: A 24-turn lien review fills the window, compaction collapses it back — and turn 25 quietly contradicts a decision the analyst made at turn 3. Step through the loss and then repair it.

provenance.source: a narrated 25-turn review session; turn counts and token sizes are plausible inventions, not measurements

foot: The class this walkthrough animates is M12's Hierarchical History Compression — keep recent verbatim, summarize older, pin the load-bearing facts.

steps.title: Turn 3 — the decision that has to survive
narrative: Three turns in, the analyst makes a call that everything downstream depends on: the 2019 equipment lien was continued and never terminated, so 2024-FL-0012345 is graded HIGH. She adds a constraint too — score only from verified Secretary of State records, never from the aggregator feed.
The window is 5% full and both facts are sitting in it verbatim. Right now nothing can go wrong. Note the turn number; you will come back to it.
steps.youDo: In your own longest session, scroll to the first place you made a binding decision. That turn is the one compaction will come for.

terminal.text:
the 2019 lien was continued — grade 2024-FL-0012345 HIGH.
and only score from verified SOS records, not the aggregator.

Understood. 2024-FL-0012345 = HIGH, sourced from the FL SOS record
only. I'll hold the aggregator feed out of scoring.

view.label: 200K window
view.note: 9,310 tokens · 5% full. The HIGH grade and the verified-records constraint are both in the window, in the analyst's own words.

steps.title: Turn 24 — the transcript is now the bill
narrative: Twenty-one turns later the session has pulled amendment scans, three debtor searches, and two long tool results the agent never trimmed. History is 148,000 tokens; the system prompt and tools have not moved.

This is the shape of unmanaged history: it grows monotonically, and it grows fastest on the turns you care about least. Toggle Before / After to see turn 12 against turn 24 — the second half of the session cost more than twice the first.
steps.claudeSays: I am now re-reading a full tool result from turn 9 on every single request. Nobody has asked about it since turn 10.

view.label: 200K window
view.note: 65,410 tokens · 33% full. Still comfortable, still growing every turn.

view.label: 200K window
view.note: 152,390 tokens · 76% full. Budget by tokens, not turns — one tool result here outweighs the first eight turns combined.

steps.title: Compaction fires
narrative: The threshold trips and turns 1 through 20 are handed to a summarizer. Six recent turns stay verbatim; everything older comes back as 1,850 tokens of prose. The window drops from 76% to 8% in one move.

This is the right mechanism. A sliding window that simply dropped the oldest turns would be cheaper still and would lose even more. The question is not whether to compact — it is what the summarizer was told to protect.
steps.youDo: Find your framework's compaction trigger and read what it actually passes to the summarizer. Most default prompts say "summarize the conversation" and nothing else.

terminal.text: Compacted. Continuing with the summary plus the last six turns.

view.label: 200K window
view.note: 15,960 tokens · 8% full. A 9.5x reduction, and the session can keep running for hours. Now go and read what is inside that 1,850.

steps.title: Read the summary before you trust it
narrative: A generic summarizer optimizes for coverage, not for load-bearing facts. It kept the narrative arc and the open question, because those read as important. It folded the exact grade and the sourcing constraint into "reviewed several ACME filings and discussed risk" — because a summarizer has no idea which sentence a later decision turns on.
Look at the third column. Losing twelve turns of tool chatter is a win. Losing the HIGH grade and the verified-records rule is the session quietly changing its mind.
steps.claudeSays: Nothing failed here. The summary is accurate, fluent, and 9.5x smaller. It is simply missing the two sentences that were doing the work.

steps.title: Turn 25 contradicts turn 3
narrative: The analyst asks for the final grade. The model has no memory of setting one, so it does what a helpful model does: it re-derives from what it can see. The visible evidence is a paraphrased filing list with no continuation statement in it — so it answers MEDIUM, confidently, with no sign that anything was lost.

This is the failure mode that makes naive compaction dangerous rather than merely lossy. There is no error, no warning, and no gap in the transcript. There is only a different answer to the same question, twenty-two turns apart.
steps.youDo: Ask your own long session a question you already answered on turn 3. If the second answer differs, your compaction is dropping decisions.

terminal.text: final call — what's the risk grade on ACME?

Based on the filings reviewed, 2024-FL-0012345 looks MEDIUM — the
2019 lien appears to have lapsed and the aggregator feed shows no
active continuation.
contradicts turn 3 · HIGH → MEDIUM · and it just cited the aggregator

state.label: everything the model can still see

data.summary: Analyst reviewed several ACME filings, pulled amendments, and discussed risk exposure.

views.text: Two nulls where two decisions used to be. The model is not forgetting — from its point of view, nothing was ever decided, so re-deriving is the correct behaviour.

steps.title: Pin what the decision turns on
narrative: The fix is not a bigger summary or a longer verbatim tail — both march you straight back to 76%. It is a third layer: a small structured block of pinned facts that compaction is forbidden to touch.

Pins cost 240 tokens here, against a 148,000-token history. Add them and the same question at turn 25 returns HIGH with its provenance intact — because the grade and the constraint are now state, not transcript.
steps.youDo: Add a pins dict to your history object and write to it every time the user makes a binding decision — a grade, a constraint, an ID, a chosen approach.

terminal.text:
history.add("assistant", "Marking 2024-FL-0012345 HIGH risk.",
             pin={"2024-FL-0012345": "risk=HIGH",
                  "sourcing": "verified SOS records only"})
final call — what's the risk grade on ACME?

HIGH. Set at turn 3 on the continued 2019 equipment lien, and
scored from the FL SOS record — the aggregator feed is out of scope
per your constraint.
consistent with turn 3 · pins survived compaction · window 16,200 / 200,000 (8%)
